jobs.title: Senior Recruiter
jobs.description:
COMPANY 

Credit Genie is a mobile-first financial wellness platform designed to help individuals take control of their financial future. We leverage artificial intelligence to provide personalized insights and are building a financial ecosystem by offering tools and services that provide instant access to cash, and building credit. Our goal is to empower every customer to achieve long-term financial stability.


Founded in 2019 by Ed Harycki https://www.linkedin.com/in/ed-harycki/, former Swift Capital Founder (acquired by PayPal in 2017 https://techcrunch.com/2017/08/10/paypal-acquires-swift-financial/). Backed by Khosla Ventures and led by industry pioneers from companies such as; PayPal, Square, and Cash App, we are well positioned to build the future of inclusive finance through cutting-edge technology and customer-centric solutions.

Overview

We are building something that matters. Our most important advantage is the people we bring in to solve this problem. This role is the foundation of how we build our organization. Talent is our most important competitive advantage, and we treat it that way. That means knowing who we want before the role opens, hiring for ceiling not credentials, and making conviction-based decisions rather than consensus-based ones. This seat sits at the center of that work.

We believe recruiting is company-building, and this seat reflects that. You will own full-cycle searches across technical and cross-functional functions, partner directly with hiring managers and EPD leadership, and be accountable for the quality of the people we bring through the door. This is a craft role. You will define the hiring thesis for each search: the one or two spikes that make a hire exceptional, not a checklist. You will build proactive pipelines before the req opens and run candidate processes with urgency and care. You won't be working off a req list. We need someone who can take high-level direction from leadership and turn it into a sharp, targeted search: knowing exactly who we want before the role even opens, building the case for it, and defending that point of view with evidence. Good enough is not good enough here. If the bar is at risk, you push back. Recruiting at Credit Genie is owned end to end, not handed off. That means staying close to the candidate, close to the hiring manager, and close to the work so context never gets lost and quality never gets diluted. We move with purpose. We own every outcome.

Responsibilities

 - Partner with EPD leaders and hiring managers to understand each role's requirements and how it fits the organization.

 - Manage full-cycle recruiting across multiple complex searches, owning every stage from first touch to signed offer.

 - Build targeted sourcing strategies. Know the companies, the teams, and the people worth pursuing before the req opens.

 - Use AI tools across sourcing, outreach, research, and pipeline as a core part of how you work, not an experiment.

 - Own your funnel metrics and the infrastructure behind them. Maintain data integrity in Ashby, know where the bottlenecks are before someone tells you, and bring evidence to calibration conversations: passthrough rates, pipeline stage data, not just gut.

 - Own offer processes end to end: extending, negotiating, closing, and generating offer letters.

 - Act as a strategic advisor. Use market intelligence to anticipate hiring needs, push back on misaligned expectations, and shift strategy when the signal changes. Translate abstract asks into concrete target lists, comp frameworks, and close plans, and bring data, not just instinct, to every conversation.

Qualifications

 - High ownership is your default, not your mode. You notice what is broken and fix it without being asked. If something in your scope is off, you own it.

 - You run every candidate process with urgency and care.

 - 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting at a high-growth startup. You have closed strong candidates in competitive markets and have the track record to show it.

 - Genuine talent judgment: You can map a market, identify the signal that separates exceptional from competent, and explain your reasoning. Your point of view is grounded in research and pattern recognition.

 - AI-fluent: AI is embedded in how you work: sourcing, outreach, research, pipeline. You can walk through your setup, explain what you have iterated on, and demonstrate what changed because of it.

Preferred

 - Scale-up and start-up experience.

 - Experience building recruiting infrastructure from scratch: intake frameworks, scorecards, sourcing playbooks.

 - Demonstrated use of AI recruiting tools as core stack with concrete before/after


BENEFITS AND PERKS

Our goal is to provide a comprehensive offering of benefits and perks that promote better financial, mental, and physical wellness.



We believe working alongside each other in person is the best way to build a great product and foster a strong company culture. Our expectation is that employees are in the office five days a week, allowing for optimal collaboration, inclusivity, and productivity. At the same time, we understand that life happens and recognize the importance of flexibility. We are committed to supporting our employees when circumstances arise that require remote work or adjusted schedules. Our goal is to ensure everyone can effectively balance personal and professional responsibilities while maintaining our collaborative and productive environment.



Here are some highlights of our benefits and perks offerings, feel free to ask your recruiting partner for more details on our comprehensive offering for employees.

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one part of your total compensation and rewards package at Credit Genie. You may also be eligible to participate in the bonus and equity programs. jobs.title: Member of Recruiting Staff - Recruiter
jobs.description:
ABOUT LIQUID AI

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.




THE OPPORTUNITY

You will own searches from intake through close across Business, Go-to-Market, G&A, People Operations, and Product. Working directly with hiring managers, business leaders, and founders, you will help build the teams that bring Liquid to customers and support our growth.

You will build your own pipeline, run your searches, manage candidate and hiring-manager relationships, and help build the recruiting function as you operate it.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We need someone who:

 - Loves the craft: You go deep on the company, role, and talent market, and form a clear view of how to find and engage the right people.

 - Owns the outcome: You identify what is holding a search back, decide what to do next, and keep it moving without waiting to be chased.

 - Builds trust on both sides: You understand what candidates and hiring managers care about, communicate directly, and push back when the evidence calls for it.




THE WORK

 - Own searches from role intake and market mapping through sourcing, assessment, interviews, offer, and close.

 - Build your own pipeline through direct sourcing, referrals, research, professional communities, events, and other creative channels, with thoughtful, individualized outreach.

 - Partner with hiring managers to define what exceptional looks like, turn ambiguous hiring needs into clear searches, and keep those searches moving.

 - Manage candidates with the close in mind from the first conversation, understand what drives their decisions, and build the case for Liquid throughout the process.

 - Run a disciplined operation in Ashby, surface stalled searches before anyone asks, and use market and pipeline evidence to improve the search.




EXPERIENCE & CAPABILITIES

What you'll need:

 - Full-cycle recruiting experience, including personally sourcing candidates and owning searches through close.

 - Depth in one or more of the hiring markets covered by this role, with a clear understanding of how to identify strong candidates.

 - Evidence that you can find and engage hard-to-reach candidates without relying on inbound or brand alone.

 - Strong candidate judgment and experience navigating competitive closes.

 - Ability to learn unfamiliar functions and markets quickly and become credible with the people you recruit.

 - Based in San Francisco and able to work from our office four days per week.

Helpful, not required:

 - Experience recruiting across multiple business or corporate functions, or for Product and Solutions Architecture roles in a technology company.

 - Early-stage experience where you helped build the recruiting function.

 - Experience with hiring-manager coaching, interview design, recruiting analytics, or complex offers.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (YEAR ONE)

 - You independently own your portfolio of searches from intake through close and consistently create your own pipeline.

 - You win competitive candidates by understanding what matters to them and making a compelling case for Liquid.

 - Hiring managers trust you as a partner in defining roles, evaluating talent, and making hiring decisions.

 - Your improvements help the team source, assess, close, or learn from hires more effectively.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Build the hiring system: Own searches from intake through close, work directly with business leadership and founders, and help shape how Liquid identifies, assesses, and closes exceptional people as we scale.

 - Compensation & Equity: Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.

 - Time Off: Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.

 - Health & Wellbeing: Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.

 - Paid Leave: Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Technical Program Manager, New Product Programs
jobs.location: Mountain View, CA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo's Commercialization & Strategic PMO Technical Program Managers are accountable for delivering Waymo's commercial business lines, platform expansion, and strategic new initiatives. We provide thoughtful cross-functional planning, clarity, and proactive risk management. When a new product has no established playbook, we act with thoughtful urgency to structure the work, drive decisions, and align teams across organizations. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Hardware, Safety, Legal, and Operations to take new initiatives from early concept to real-world launch.

This role follows a hybrid work schedule, and you will report to the Director of Technical Program Management, Commercialization & Strategic PMO.

You will:

• Architect and lead the holistic, cross-organizational technical program for Waymo's New Product Programs initiatives

• Own and drive the end-to-end program structure, work breakdown, and master schedule across pillars, delegating sub-projects across domain TPMs while retaining accountability for the holistic program and its interdependencies.

• Serve as a strategic technical partner to Product and Engineering leadership across TaaS, Fleet & Operations, Onboard Autonomy, Hardware, and Systems/Safety Engineering

• Simplify interfaces across organizational boundaries by establishing scalable operating frameworks, cross-org structures, and readiness playbooks.

• Occasional travel between Bay Area offices, test facilities/depots, OEM partner sites, or expansion markets, about one week per quarter (~10%).

You have:

• 10+ years of experience leading transformational, multi-organization technical programs from 0-to-1 conception through public launch and scaled operations across hardware, embedded/onboard software, cloud/mobile platforms, and physical operations.

• Demonstrated technical judgment equivalent to a senior/staff practicing engineer (L5+ SWE): ability to influence strategic technical direction, evaluate complex system architectures across onboard and offboard stacks, and broker high-stakes velocity vs. quality decisions.

• A proven track record of structuring ambiguous, company-level initiatives into unambiguous work breakdowns, milestones, and accountability frameworks while managing a portfolio of interdependent workstreams and guiding other TPMs.

• Deep experience in resource management, capacity forecasting, and financial/unit-economics modeling across large distributed engineering organizations (100+ engineers) without direct line authority.

• Experience navigating safety-critical, regulated, or hardware-software integrated consumer products where product readiness, verification & validation (V&V), and field operations must converge on strict release cadences.

• Exceptional executive presence and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence VP/C-level leadership, align multidisciplinary leads (Engineering, Product, Legal, Safety, Operations, OEM Partnerships), and drive organizational change.

We prefer:

• Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive OEM platform programs, robotics, aerospace, or complex consumer hardware-software ecosystems with long hardware freeze lead times.

• A track record of taking a net-new business line or incubation program inside a scaled technology company from early prototype/fishfood to external customer pilot and commercial agreement.

• Familiarity with automotive regulatory and homologation frameworks (DMV, CPUC, NHTSA, FMVSS, multi-stage manufacturing), consumer auto insurance/underwriting, or physical fleet/depot operations.

• Experience mentoring, coordinating, and scaling a cohort of Technical Program Managers across multiple functional pillars (e.g., Onboard, Cloud/Mobile, Fleet, Release/Safety).

ABOUT US

Conversion is the agentic marketing automation platform for modern enterprises such as Plaid, ClickHouse, Webflow, and Productboard. Our platform lets growth teams run their entire go-to-market motion in one place, from acquisition through retention, with AI agents doing the work that legacy tools like Marketo, HubSpot, and Pardot can't.

We've raised $28M+ from Abstract Ventures, True Ventures, and HOF Capital. The team is based in San Francisco and includes engineers, designers, and operators from Airbnb, Palantir, Pinterest, IMC, Shopify, LinkedIn, and Microsoft.

 

About the Role

Hey there! James here 👋, co-founder and CTO at Conversion. Just wanted to share my thoughts on the perfect candidate we're looking to join our product engineering team. Whether you lean backend, frontend, or work across both, we'd love to hear from you.

 - Product focused: There are a lot of features that go into a marketing automation platform, and we're looking for engineers who can own entire products and scope out, design, and build them end to end. We believe the best PMs are engineers who understand the pain point, since they can best evaluate both the benefit and the cost of building a feature.

 - Love building for / with customers: We're extremely close with our customers. Every customer gets their own Slack channel in our org, and we add every engineer to the channel to directly answer questions, fix bugs, and ship features. A key component of this role will be working with customers to understand pain points and then researching / designing the product features to solve them!

 - Detail oriented: Conversion's product is a deeply integrated platform where each feature must mesh seamlessly with many existing features and support an ambitious vision. A detail oriented approach is required to keep our high bar for craft while delivering complex features in a scalable way.

 - Intellectually curious: Conversion engineers are the kind of people who get excited about a weird edge case and end up sending five Slack messages about it before lunch.

 

Concrete Responsibilities:

 - Vision: Owning the vision and product features end to end

 - Product context: Deeply understanding our customers and the enterprise marketing space

 - Product engineering: Owning the end to end delivery of the product from customer need to final product shipped

This role is in-person 5 days/week in San Francisco.

 

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

 - Have 3+ years of industry experience shipping product features

 - Have a startup mindset and want early ownership in a fast-paced environment

 - Have experience with our tech stack:
   
   - Go for backend services

You Might Be a Great Fit If You

 - Have worked at a Series A to C startup that scaled quickly

 - Care about owning the delivery of a feature end to end and continuing to ensure customers are happy even after delivery

 - Have a strong track record of side projects, apps, or hackathons. Our engineers have built a live-streaming security system for their parents' new house, a database from scratch, a better Splitwise app, and hosted our Minecraft server, all while at Conversion

jobs.title: Director of Total Rewards
jobs.description:
Meriton is a national team of experts driving HVAC innovation through a network of high-performing companies. From strategy and support to systems and solutions, we work behind the scenes to strengthen operations and build value—for our partners and our people.

If you’re looking to make an impact, we’re glad you’re here. At Meriton, you’ll join a team that believes in big ideas, doing great work, and building careers that matter—every step of the way.

The Director of Total Rewards leads the enterprise Total Rewards function and is accountable for the strategy, design, governance, compliance, financial stewardship, and employee experience of Meriton’s benefits, compensation, retirement, leave, and wellbeing programs across all operating companies. This role ensures Total Rewards programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, cost-effective, and aligned with business growth, talent retention, M&A integration, and organizational performance priorities.

The Director of Total Rewards serves as the enterprise subject matter leader and strategic advisor to executive leadership, operating company leaders, HR, Payroll, HRIS, Finance, Legal, and external partners. The role drives a mature, data-informed rewards strategy through executive-ready recommendations, disciplined governance, vendor performance management, regulatory oversight, cross-functional alignment, and leadership of the Total Rewards team.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

• Establish and execute the enterprise Total Rewards strategy, roadmap, governance model, and service delivery standards across benefits, compensation, retirement, leave, wellbeing, and related rewards programs for all operating companies.

• Direct the design, administration, governance, and optimization of health & welfare, retirement, disability, life, voluntary, wellbeing, and leave programs for a multi-state, multi-OpCo workforce. Lead annual open enrollment strategy, plan design decisions, communications, system readiness, vendor coordination, funding recommendations, and executive reporting.

• Own the enterprise vendor ecosystem, including brokers, carriers, TPAs, recordkeepers, retirement advisors, consultants, and equity partners. Lead high-impact negotiations, RFP strategy, renewal decisions, performance scorecards, service escalations, contract governance, and cost containment initiatives to ensure service quality, financial discipline, and alignment with enterprise standards.

• Direct enterprise compliance strategy for benefits, compensation, retirement, leave, and related Total Rewards programs in a multi-state environment. Monitor federal, state, and local regulatory developments; sponsor timely implementation; and maintain governance routines, documentation, policies, procedures, controls, audits, Form 5500 filings, ACA reporting, participant notices, and regulatory inquiry responses to ensure audit readiness and risk mitigation.

• Lead enterprise compensation strategy, including job architecture, leveling, salary structures, incentive plan governance, market benchmarking, pay equity practices, offer guidance, and executive-ready compensation analytics. Partner with HR, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and business leaders to ensure compensation decisions support internal equity, market competitiveness, compliance, retention, and business affordability.

• Serve as business owner for Total Rewards technology, reporting, and analytics across HCM, benefits administration, retirement, compensation, and related platforms. Partner with HRIS, IT, Payroll, Finance, and vendors to improve integrations, controls, workflows, data quality, automation, dashboards, employee self-service, and decision-ready insights.

• Lead Total Rewards due diligence, risk assessment, executive recommendations, and integration strategy for mergers, acquisitions, and new operating company onboarding. Establish scalable integration playbooks, transition approaches, benefit harmonization recommendations, compensation alignment frameworks, and post-close service delivery models that protect compliance, continuity of coverage, and employee experience.

• Partner with Finance, Payroll, Accounting, and executive leadership to provide financial stewardship for enterprise Total Rewards programs, including funding, reconciliation, forecasting, budgeting, cost modeling, liability analysis, premium strategy, retirement contributions, and long-range planning. Use analytics to inform recommendations, manage risk, and support sustainable rewards investments.

• Influence and align cross-functional stakeholders across HR, Finance, Accounting, Legal, Payroll, HRIS, Talent Acquisition, OpCo leadership, and external partners to ensure Total Rewards strategies, policies, processes, and communications support enterprise priorities, operating company needs, regulatory requirements, and a consistent employee experience.

Director of Total Rewards Competencies

• Strategic Total Rewards leader who connects rewards design, governance, compliance, and financial stewardship to enterprise growth, workforce retention, talent attraction, and operating company integration.

• Deep subject matter expertise across broad-based compensation, executive and incentive compensation governance, health & welfare, retirement, leave, wellbeing, ERISA, ACA, fiduciary oversight, audits, and multi-state compliance.

• Executive communicator who converts complex compensation, benefits, retirement, compliance, financial, and employee experience considerations into clear recommendations, decision points, risk assessments, and implementation plans.

• Trusted advisor who builds credibility with executives, operating company leaders, HR, Finance, Payroll, Legal, vendors, and employees through sound judgment, collaboration, discretion, and follow-through.

• Operational leader with strong command of controls, data integrity, confidentiality, audit readiness, service delivery, documentation, and measurable continuous improvement.

• Change leader who can prioritize competing enterprise initiatives, manage ambiguity, anticipate risk, and guide teams through transformation in a fast-paced, acquisition-oriented environment.

Education/Experience:

• Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Accounting, or related field; equivalent professional experience also considered

• Minimum 10+ years of progressive Total Rewards leadership experience, including enterprise-level ownership of benefits, compensation, retirement, leave, wellbeing, compliance, vendor governance, and rewards strategy in a multi-state, multi-unit, or shared services environment

• Demonstrated experience advising executive leaders, presenting Board- or executive-ready recommendations, leading Total Rewards teams, managing enterprise vendor partnerships, overseeing fiduciary and regulatory governance, and driving scalable rewards transformation

• Certified Benefits Professional (CBP) or similar designation preferred

• Demonstrated experience managing & supporting health & welfare benefits and retirement plans in multi-state, multi-unit operations

• M&A benefits & compensation integration expertise preferred

• Experience with major HCM/benefit administration platforms (e.g., Workday, ADP, UKG, Oracle, Dayforce, or similar).

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essentials functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. The workplace is in a corporate office environment and the temperature in the work environment is usually moderate. jobs.title: PLANEADOR DE CONTROL DE PROCESOS (AGROINDUSTRIA)
jobs.description:
Planificar y controlar la producción de acuerdo con la demanda comercial, la disponibilidad de materias primas, la capacidad instalada, los inventarios y los requerimientos de embarque, asegurando el cumplimiento oportuno de los compromisos del negocio, la continuidad operativa y el uso eficiente de los recursos.

Alcance del rol: integrar la información comercial y operativa para convertirla en planes ejecutables de producción, anticipar restricciones y facilitar decisiones oportunas entre Producción, Almacenes, Calidad, Logística, Comercial, Compras, Mantenimiento y Finanzas.

Dimensión y contexto

Financiero: No administra necesariamente un presupuesto directo; sin embargo, sus decisiones impactan la utilización de capacidad, productividad, niveles de inventario, costos operativos, horas extra, reprocesos y cumplimiento de compromisos comerciales.

Staff: Sin reportes directos, salvo que la estructura organizacional vigente determine lo contrario.

Interacción funcional: Producción, Almacenes, Calidad, Logística, Comercial, Compras, Mantenimiento, Finanzas, SHE y demás áreas vinculadas con la ejecución del plan.

Otros: Gestiona información de demanda, órdenes de producción, inventarios, disponibilidad de materia prima, empaques, certificaciones, capacidad y fechas de embarque.

Principales responsabilidades

• Planificación de la producción: Desarrollar y mantener el plan de producción, alineando la demanda comercial y los requerimientos de embarque con la capacidad disponible, las prioridades del negocio y las restricciones operativas.
• Conversión de demanda: Convertir los requerimientos comerciales en necesidades de producción, considerando volúmenes, calidades, certificaciones, especificaciones de producto, presentaciones y fechas comprometidas.
• Disponibilidad de materia prima: Monitorear la cobertura y disponibilidad de materia prima para asegurar la continuidad del programa, anticipando faltantes y escalando oportunamente los riesgos.
• Capacidad y restricciones: Evaluar la capacidad productiva y las restricciones de equipos, personal, almacenamiento y servicios, identificando cuellos de botella y alternativas de ejecución.
• Control del programa: Dar seguimiento al cumplimiento del plan de producción, analizar desviaciones entre lo planificado y lo ejecutado y coordinar los ajustes requeridos.
• Coordinación interfuncional: Alinear con Producción, Almacenes, Calidad, Comercial, Logística y áreas de soporte la secuencia, prioridades y condiciones necesarias para ejecutar el plan.
• Materiales y empaques: Planificar y monitorear las necesidades de materiales, empaques e insumos vinculados con la producción, anticipando riesgos para la continuidad operativa.
• Indicadores de gestión: Monitorear y analizar indicadores de cumplimiento del plan, utilización de capacidad, disponibilidad de inventario, adherencia al programa y nivel de servicio.
• Escenarios y toma de decisiones: Preparar escenarios de producción y capacidad ante cambios en demanda, inventarios, prioridades comerciales, mantenimiento o restricciones operativas.
• Calidad de datos y reportes: Mantener actualizada, consistente y trazable la información de planeación en los sistemas y herramientas de gestión utilizados por la organización.
• Mejora continua: Identificar e impulsar oportunidades de productividad, automatización, estandarización e innovación en los procesos de planeación y control.
• Sistemas de gestión: Cumplir y contribuir con los lineamientos de SHE, Calidad, Inocuidad, Seguridad Patrimonial y el Sistema Integrado de Gestión aplicables al puesto.

Ingeniero Industrial o carrera afin

Que ofrecemos

Un entorno multicultural, dinámico y desafiante, que ampliará y desarrollará sus capacidades y canalizará sus habilidades y experiencia con excelentes oportunidades de desarrollo profesional, en una de las companías mas sólidas a nivel global.

Estos son algunos de nuestros beneficios:

-Salario y Beneficios Competitivos.

-Ambiente Laboral Flexible.

-Accesos a Capacitaciones y Desarrollo.

-Programa de Salud y Bienestar.

-Licencia por Maternidad y Paternidad Extendida.

Diversidad & Inclusión

LDC se rige por un conjunto de valores compartidos, elevadas normas éticas, y la diversidad y la inclusión forman parte de nuestro ADN. LDC es una empresa que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades y se compromete a proporcionar un entorno de trabajo que adopte y valore la diversidad, la equidad y la inclusión.

LDC fomenta la diversidad, apoya a las comunidades locales y las iniciativas medioambientales. Animamos a personas de todos los orígenes a presentar su candidatura.

Sustentabilidad

El valor sustentable está en el centro de nuestro propósito como empresa.

Nos apasiona crear un valor justo y sustentable, tanto para nuestra empresa como para las demás partes interesadas de la cadena de valor: nuestra gente, nuestros socios comerciales, las comunidades con las que nos relacionamos y el medioambiente que nos rodea.

jobs.title: Director Post-Si Electrical Validation Engineering
jobs.description:
Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB) provides rack-scale AI infrastructure through purpose-built connectivity solutions. By collaborating with hyperscalers and ecosystem partners, Astera Labs enables organizations to unlock the full potential of modern AI. Astera Labs’ Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates CXL®, Ethernet, NVLink, PCIe®, and UALink™ semiconductor-based technologies with the company’s COSMOS software suite to unify diverse components into cohesive, flexible systems that deliver end-to-end scale-up, and scale-out connectivity. The company’s custom connectivity solutions business complements its standards-based portfolio, enabling customers to deploy tailored architectures to meet their unique infrastructure requirements. Discover more at www.asteralabs.com.

Astera Labs is seeking a Director of Post-Si Electrical Validation Engineering to lead the development, bring-up, and validation of ASIC SerDes and PCIe PHY products that enable rack-scale AI infrastructure. Working closely with ASIC, systems, firmware, signal integrity, power integrity, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and customer engineering teams, you will guide products from concept and architecture through qualification and mass production.

This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving environment. You will lead a talented engineering team while stepping in to solve complex technical problems, engage directly with customers, and improve hardware development processes. Your work will help ensure Astera Labs’ connectivity and memory products deliver reliable, high-performance systems for cloud service providers, server manufacturers, and networking OEMs.

Key Responsibilities

• Board Product Strategy and Technical Leadership

• Lead ASIC Electrical-level (PHY) validation strategy across product definition, architecture, PCB/test fixture development, Validation Automation, data review, bring-up, debug, optimization, qualification, and production release.

• Define validation plans, coverage goals, risk assessments, schedules, and exit criteria for high-speed ASIC and PHY IP

• Make hands-on technical contributions to unblock critical design, validation, and customer issues in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

• High-Speed SerDes Validation

• Direct ASIC Power-On and bring-up, silicon/PCB debug, PVT characterization, margin analysis, and performance optimization across voltage, temperature, channel, and workload conditions.

• Validate high-speed NRZ and PAM4 SerDes-based protocols, including PCIe Gen 3 and above

• Apply signal/power integrity, SerDes/PHY knowledge, coding, and lab expertise to identify risks and drive practical solutions across circuits, power distribution, connectors, sockets, and cables.

• Cross-Functional and Customer Execution

• Partner with ASIC, system validation, firmware, systems, mechanical, thermal, quality, compliance, manufacturing, and customer engineering teams to deliver robust products.

• Engage key internal customers to understand system requirements, evaluate form factors, propose complete board solutions, and resolve issues through production support.

• Collaborate with external vendors for test equipment, bench sockets, temperature forcing units, RF cables, PCB vendors, and related suppliers to ensure validation platforms are automated, robust, and scalable.

• Team Development and Productization

• Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing engineering team while establishing clear ownership, technical standards, and execution mechanisms.

• Drive products from concept to mass production, including validation data reviews, code/automatin reviews, validation reporting, documentation, and post-production support.

• Improve post-Silicon development processes and methodologies, share lessons learned, and reuse validation best practices across Astera Labs’ connectivity and memory product portfolio.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field. Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering preferred.

• 12 - 15+ years of relevant experience, consistent with Astera Labs’ standardized Director level.

• Technical management experience leading design, validation, product, or system engineering teams.

• Experience with high-speed serdes PHY Validation over PVT conditions and taking products from concept to validation plan, validation, production release and post-production support.

• Strong background in high-speed SerDes IP validation and PHY tuning, signal/power integrity, and automation using common lab equipment such as high-speed oscilloscopes, BERTs, and VNAs

• Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and can-do attitude. Think and act with the customer in mind!

• Strong cross-functional collaboration, technical communication, prioritization, and independent problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications.

• Experience leading SoC Debug and development for high-speed interfaces such as PCIe5, PCIe6 or PAM4 802.3 Ethernet.

• Working knowledge of key, high-speed PHY design blocks such as PLL’s, DFE, Tx EQ,FFE, CDR, etc and signaling concepts such as PAM4

• Strong python scripting ability: knowledge of object-oriented programming and basic dev ops using git for source control and collaboration

• Deep background in developing bench automation techniques, preferably using Python, with emphasis on execution efficiency, repeatability, and data analysis.

• Proficiency using high-speed lab equipment such as BERT, Oscilloscope, and VNA

• Startup experience and a proactive, hands-on, customer-focused approach to solving complex problems.

Salary range is $210,000 to $275,000 depending on experience, level, and business need. This role may be eligible for discretionary bonus, incentives and benefits.

You'll work directly with Perplexity's senior leadership to spearhead a broad portfolio of strategic technology initiatives across policy, law, operations, and corporate affairs.

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Policy & Strategic Initiatives group, you'll occupy a front-row seat to the foremost policy issues animating the AI ecosystem. You'll also get a panoptic view of how leading AI companies operate, make decisions, and engage with broader society.

Those seeking to marry technical expertise and broader interests in law, policy, and corporate affairs will find a home in this role. You'll make contributions to Perplexity that defy traditional boundaries, with a bench of mentors who will push you to learn and grow day after day.







WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Your work will be both highly interdisciplinary and firmly grounded in engineering rigor. On any given day, you might:

 - Harness AI agents to research high-stakes policy and regulatory issues pertaining to Perplexity.

 - Build automated platforms for harvesting, prioritizing, and patenting Perplexity's inventions, in collaboration with our AI researchers and intellectual property attorneys.

 - Work hands-on with our Legal team and outside counsel in support of high-tech litigation matters in U.S. federal court.

 - Engineer privacy and compliance systems that efficiently scale with our growing portfolio of frontier AI products (such as Comet https://www.perplexity.ai/comet and Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).

 - Contribute to regulatory filings and responses that require impeccable command of AI technology, Perplexity's own systems, and the broader policy landscape.

 - Embed with our People team to implement first-party software solutions for recruiting, labor compliance, and performance management.

 - Participate in meetings with Capitol Hill, executive branch officials, international partners, and civil society as a subject-matter expert on both AI technology and policy.

The above is a small sampling of activities; no two days will be the same, and your work will take you to all corners of our company. You'll interact each day with Perplexity's senior leaders, who will come to rely on you as a creative problem solver for simple and complex matters alike.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

No single profile defines our ideal candidate for this role. Here are some examples of people who might thrive here:

 - Exceptionally talented early-career engineers (new grads welcome) who are (1) well-read in law, tech policy, or economics, and (2) wish to grow in both technical and non-technical disciplines.
   
   - We welcome candidates who plan to attend law school or PhD programs in the future; we ask for a minimum 2-year commitment (i.e., you would apply for the entering class of 2028 or later).

 - Experienced engineers at top tech companies who wish to develop policy, business, and operations chops.

 - Lawyers or economists (new JD or PhD grads welcome) who've kept their engineering skills sharp and are excited to reimagine their fields in the age of AI.

 - This is a non-exhaustive list; other profiles may also be great fits.

No matter which profile describes you, we'll also be looking for:

 - Evidence of exceptional ability and 99th-percentile work ethic.

 - Strong technical skills at or above Perplexity's hiring bar for software engineers.

 - Fluency with frontier intelligence tools (such as Perplexity Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).

 - High intrinsically-enforced standards for the craft and quality of your work.

 - Strong communication and writing skills, ideally demonstrated via samples of past written work product.

 - Curiosity and excitement about new and unfamiliar fields; eagerness to redefine your job every 3-6 months.

 - Ability to quickly dive deep in any given field and develop mastery rivaling that of domain experts.

 - Unimpeachable judgment, integrity, and discretion to be entrusted with the company's most important matters.

 - A service-oriented attitude that continually questions how company systems and processes might better serve stakeholders.

jobs.title: Facility Manager
jobs.description:
About the Company

General Matter is enriching uranium in America.

Our goal is to design, build, and operate the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services in the United States.

Our mission is to restore America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel—fuel that will power AI, advanced manufacturing, critical industries, and the next generation of nuclear reactors.

Ultimately, our work will help power national ambitions and enable a high-energy society.

We were incubated by Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by top-tier investors. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.

We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.

Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.

About This Role

As Facility Manager at General Matter, reporting to the Site Manager, you'll build and lead the facilities function for a roughly 87-acre industrial site in Paducah, Kentucky, that we're bringing back into service for nuclear-industry process piping and steel fabrication. The site has several manufacturing buildings plus support buildings for offices, storage, utilities and shop services. Much of its infrastructure needs to be assessed, restored and recommissioned before production can start.

Most facilities managers inherit a running plant and keep it running. This role is different: it's a start-up. You'll restore legacy power, water, compressed air, natural gas, HVAC and fire protection systems, and sequence the work so each building is ready before production or occupancy arrives. You'll also build a facilities team of about 15 people from the ground up and decide with site leadership which services stay in-house and which are contracted. Your decisions on utility capacity and building readiness will directly set how fast the site can deliver the hardware behind America's new enrichment capacity.

If you seek high impact and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to apply to join our team.

Responsibilities

Infrastructure Restoration & Capital Projects

• Assess and restore legacy power distribution, water, compressed air, natural gas, HVAC, fire protection and building envelope across every manufacturing and support building; build and execute the infrastructure restoration plan.

• Plan and manage facility capital projects and renovations, including the office building build-out: scope work, select and manage contractors, control budget and schedule, and close out projects.

• Sequence work across buildings so each is ready ahead of its production or occupancy date.

Utilities, Grounds & Site Services

• Manage utility service, metering and energy use, and coordinate with providers on capacity for production equipment, welding power and cranes.

• Maintain roads, rail and truck access, laydown and storage yards, drainage, snow removal and the site perimeter across the property.

• Run custodial, waste and recycling, pest control and space services across all manufacturing and support buildings.

Compliance & Nuclear Readiness

• Keep fire protection, egress, emergency lighting and pressure systems inspected and compliant; work with EHS on permits, environmental requirements and emergency response.

• Support site readiness for a nuclear quality and safety program (10 CFR Part 70), including controlled changes to facilities and the records that go with them.

Team, Budget & Systems

• Recruit and develop facilities technicians and utilities, grounds and custodial staff; make in-house vs. contracted service recommendations.

• Set up the facilities preventive maintenance and work order process in the site's maintenance management system, working closely with Maintenance on shared assets.

• Build and manage the facilities operating budget and service contracts; track KPIs on cost, work order backlog and response time.

Basic Qualifications

• Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc.).

• Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals.

• Ability to perform trade studies and make clear recommendations using first principles and engineering fundamentals, even with partial information.

• Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, facilities management or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 8+ years in facilities management for industrial or manufacturing sites, including 3+ years leading facilities teams and contractors.

• Hands-on knowledge of industrial electrical distribution, HVAC, compressed air, water/wastewater and fire protection systems.

• Experience restoring, renovating or recommissioning older industrial buildings or bringing a facility back into service.

• Proven ability to manage capital projects and contractors: scope, bids, budget, schedule and closeout.

• Working knowledge of OSHA, NFPA and local building and fire code requirements.

• Experience with a computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) for work orders and PMs.

• Must be a U.S. person, as this role requires regular access to export-controlled environments, and able to obtain and maintain the site access authorization required for the role.

• Ability to travel up to approximately 25%, including to other company sites, suppliers and vendors, and to respond to after-hours facility emergencies.

• Able to regularly walk multiple large buildings, roofs, utility spaces and grounds in all weather, wearing required PPE and climbing ladders, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

• This position is based onsite in Paducah, Kentucky.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Experience in a fast-paced engineering or highly technical environment, with a resourceful approach to delivering under tight timelines or budget constraints.

• Experience standing up a new facilities organization or opening a new or restarted site.

• Facilities experience in a nuclear, defense, chemical or other highly regulated industrial setting.

• Professional certification such as CFM, FMP or a PE license.

• Experience running multi-building campuses, rail-served sites or heavy-industry yards.

• Energy management or utility-cost reduction experience.

Equal Opportunity Employer

General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Compensation and Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $90,000–$175,000 annually.

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at General Matter. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock options. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, HSA/FSA/Commuter benefits, and various other benefits.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager: Extensible Compute
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


SENIOR PRODUCT MANAGER: EXTENSIBLE COMPUTE

Location: MPK or Bellevue | 
Workplace: Hybrid

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don't just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset, rapidly testing emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential, and people too. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology and careers to the next level.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager for our Extensible Compute team, which builds Snowpark Container Services (SPCS). SPCS is the compute platform that runs customer container workloads and Snowflake's own first-party products, including Openflow, Notebooks, Streamlit, and AI agents. You will own the product for that platform: which compute we offer, how reliably and cheaply it runs, and how partner teams and customers get what they need without a one-off every time.

AS A SENIOR PRODUCT MANAGER AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the SPCS product roadmap and ship it. That includes the compute instance portfolio across AWS, Azure, and GCP (general-purpose CPU, ARM, and GPU, including new Nvidia generations), and the storage and file system capabilities workloads depend on.

 - Turn requests from first-party product partners into platform capabilities. When Openflow, Notebooks, Streamlit, or an agent team needs a new instance, a networking change, or multi-cluster support, you decide what becomes a standard SPCS feature and what stays a one-off.

 - Take features from early preview to general availability. You set the launch bar, hold a release when security, reliability, or unit economics are not ready, and work the path through PrPr and PuPr with engineering. Work credibly with senior engineers on architecture, performance, reliability, and cost.

 - Own platform health that customers feel: startup time, isolation, storage reliability, and the unit economics of running a workload on SPCS. You partner with Finance on pricing ($/GiB, instance pricing) when the model has to change.

 - Be the product point of contact for our infrastructure partners (AWS, Azure, GCP, Nvidia) on the SPCS compute roadmap, and for account teams qualifying strategic customers onto SPCS.

 - Use AI as part of how you work: customer and partner synthesis, specs, launch reviews, and the analysis behind a prioritization call.

OUR IDEAL SENIOR PRODUCT MANAGER WILL HAVE:

 - 5+ years of product management experience, including several years on a platform, infrastructure, or developer-facing product, or equivalent experience owning a technical product end to end.

 - Hands-on depth in at least one of: cloud infrastructure, container or serverless platforms, developer runtimes, or distributed systems. You can hold a design review with senior engineers and leave with a decision.

 - A track record of taking a platform capability from 0 to 1 or from early adoption to scale, across engineering and at least one partner team (product, GTM, or a cloud/hardware partner).

 - Evidence you can say no. You have turned a pile of bespoke asks into a smaller set of reusable capabilities, and you can show what you cut and why.

 - Clear writing and crisp communication with engineering leads, partner PMs, finance, and account teams. You do not need a slide to make the point.

 - A Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent experience.

BONUS POINTS

 - Direct experience with a container platform, Kubernetes-based service, or serverless compute product that customers run production workloads on.

 - Experience qualifying or launching GPU or accelerated compute instances, or working a hardware/CSP roadmap (Nvidia, AWS, Azure, GCP).

 - Experience supporting data, AI, or developer workloads on a shared platform (orchestration, notebooks, apps, agents).

 - Familiarity with unit economics for compute or storage: instance pricing, $/GiB, or cost-to-serve for a multi-tenant platform.

WHY JOIN OUR EXTENSIBLE COMPUTE TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

SPCS is the compute layer under a large and growing set of Snowflake workloads. A good call on an instance type, a filesystem, or a launch gate shows up in more than one product. You will work directly with the engineers who build it, the product partners who depend on it, and the customers bringing container workloads onto Snowflake.

Customers want to run their own services, pipelines, and models inside Snowflake's governance boundary, and Snowflake's own products need the same platform to get faster, cheaper, and more capable. You will have a concrete surface to own, a roadmap you can ship against, and visibility into how this platform is used across the company.



Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

Location: Remote — United States
Security Clearance: Active Secret required

Connect Critical Systems. Shape Federal Healthcare Technology.

Rackner is seeking an experienced Lead Solutions Architect to design and guide secure technology integrations supporting federal healthcare operations.

In this role, you'll lead architecture decisions connecting ServiceNow with enterprise applications, clinical systems, and operational platforms through approved APIs. You'll help establish engineering standards, guide integration efforts, and ensure technical solutions are reliable, maintainable, and aligned with security and operational requirements.

This opportunity offers the chance to influence complex technical environments, collaborate with engineering and government stakeholders, and solve meaningful integration challenges that support healthcare delivery and mission readiness.

What You'll Do

• Lead end-to-end solutions architecture and maintain the inventory of system integrations and interfaces.

• Design secure API integrations connecting ServiceNow with enterprise, clinical, and operational systems while preserving existing systems of record.

• Design ServiceNow Integration Hub spokes and integration patterns that support complex operational environments.

• Develop architecture approaches for mobile and disconnected operations, including transaction queuing, synchronization, and data reconciliation.

• Establish engineering standards and provide technical guidance to automation and data integration engineers.

• Review production releases for alignment with approved architecture, integration standards, and operational requirements.

• Identify and address technical dependencies involving platform access, licensing, security, and system interoperability.

• Develop practical alternatives when platform limitations or technical constraints affect implementation.

• Lead customer interface approval activities and represent the engineering team in architecture and security review boards.

Required Qualifications

• 8+ years of professional solutions architecture experience, including enterprise API design.

• ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) certification.

• ServiceNow Certified Application Developer (CAD) certification.

• Compliance with applicable DoD 8140 qualification requirements.

• Active U.S. Government Secret security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting Platform One or DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) environments.

Why Rackner?

At Rackner, we bring together modern engineering practices, technical expertise, and mission-focused problem-solving to support complex federal programs.

We value collaboration, practical innovation, continuous learning, and people who take ownership of their work. Our team provides opportunities to grow professionally, contribute to meaningful projects, and work alongside experienced technical and operational professionals.

jobs.title: Engagement Manager (NYC)
jobs.description:
ABOUT US



At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.









ABOUT THE TEAM:

The Professional Services team is the bridge between LangChain's technology and the enterprise customers building on top of it. We partner with some of the world's most ambitious companies to help them move from pilot to production — designing solutions, accelerating time-to-value, and ensuring teams get the most out of LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith. We work at the intersection of deep technical expertise and customer partnership, and we take pride in the outcomes our customers achieve. As LangChain grows, PS plays a direct role in shaping how enterprise AI gets built in the real world.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

We're looking for an Engagement Manager to join our Professional Services team. You'll manage multiple concurrent technical engagements, ensuring successful delivery of Professional Services projects for enterprise customers. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver exceptional outcomes.

This role offers direct impact on customer success, the opportunity to shape processes and methodologies, and the chance to work with cutting-edge AI technology. You'll join a collaborative team environment with a strong engineering culture.

Location: This role can be based in our San Francisco or New York office. Employees within commuting distance work from the office five days per week. Candidates who live outside commuting distance (e.g. >1hr each way) may be eligible for hybrid arrangements depending on location and role requirements. Open to remote candidates within the US.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Engagement Lifecycle Management: Manage the full engagement lifecycle from SOW review through closeout, including planning, execution, risk management, scope management, and handoff

 - Customer Communication & Relationship Management: Serve as the primary point of contact for customers — deliver status updates, manage expectations, handle escalations, and negotiate scope changes

 - Multi-Engagement Management: Manage 5–8 concurrent technical engagements simultaneously while maintaining quality and meeting deadlines

 - Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate with Solution Architects, AI Engineers, Sales, Support, Enablement, and Product/Engineering teams; manage resource allocation and capacity planning

 - Risk & Issue Management: Proactively identify risks and issues, develop mitigation strategies, track resolution, and ensure deliverables meet quality standards
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - You have 5+ years of engagement or project management experience, preferably with technical or software engagements

 - You've managed multiple concurrent engagements and know how to keep quality high across all of them

 - You have strong experience working with enterprise customers and leading customer-facing communication

 - You've coordinated cross-functional technical teams — engineers, architects, product — and managed resource allocation

 - You're experienced with project management tools such as Linear, Jira, Asana, or similar

 - You've handled scope change management and complex stakeholder dynamics

 - You have start-up DNA: you thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and don't wait to be told what to do

 - You're a natural communicator — clear, direct, and effective with both technical teams and executive stakeholders

You exemplify our operating principles

 - You are motivated to build something great: you hold a high bar for quality, craft, and impact

 - You embrace hot takes: you share informed opinions, challenge the status quo, and engage in constructive debate

 - You operate with maximum agency: you take ownership, move work forward independently, and help others unblock

 - You run to the roar: you lean into hard problems, ambiguity, and fast-moving challenges


NICE TO HAVE:

 - PMP or similar project management certification

 - Experience in Professional Services or consulting

 - Experience with AI/ML or infrastructure engagements

 - Experience with time tracking and billing coordination

 - Knowledge of software development lifecycle and agile methodologies
   
   


COMPENSATION 

Annual Salary: $150,000-$190,000

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.




BENEFITS

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

jobs.description:
About Pacaso

Pacaso exists to enrich lives by making second home ownership possible and enjoyable for more people. We've reimagined the second home category — pairing a thoughtfully designed co-ownership model with simplified financials, equitable scheduling, and dedicated local property management, so owners get the joy of a true second home without the hassle.

Since launch, Pacaso has facilitated more than $1.2 billion in gross real estate transactions and service fees across 40+ destinations in the U.S., Mexico, and Europe — including Aspen, Lake Tahoe, Napa, Malibu, Palm Springs, Cabo, Paris, London, and most recently Florence, Milan, and Rome. We've raised over $300 million in cumulative equity funding, closed the largest real estate Regulation A+ offering of 2025, and reserved the Nasdaq ticker PCSO as we build toward a public listing.

Our work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Fortune, Forbes, CNBC, Bloomberg, and others.

Recognition

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for both our culture and our category-defining work:

• No. 5, Forbes America's Best Startup Employers (2026) — our second consecutive Top 10 ranking

• Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2025)

• Winner, 2025 Inman Best of Proptech Awards — Consumer Experience & Marketplace Innovation

• Fortune & Great Place To Work Best Workplaces in Real Estate (2024)

• Best Workplace in the Bay Area™ (2023)

• LinkedIn Top Startup (2022) · Glassdoor Best Places to Work, #6 (2022)

Contract Groundskeeper/Porter

Company: Pacaso
Location: Park City, Utah
Position Type: Independent Contractor / Part-Time
Compensation: $30 per hour
Schedule: Recurring weekly visits to approximately 13 Pacaso properties

About the Role

Pacaso is seeking a reliable, detail-oriented Groundskeeper / Porter to support the upkeep and general presentation of our Park City home portfolio.

This role is responsible for conducting routine weekly visits to approximately 13 residential properties, ensuring each home and its surrounding exterior spaces remain clean, organized, and well-maintained.

The ideal candidate is hands-on, dependable, proactive, and comfortable working independently across multiple residential properties.

This is a flexible, hourly contract opportunity that does not require full-time availability.

Key Responsibilities

• Routine Property Upkeep

• Visit each assigned Pacaso property once per week.

• Manage trash and recycling, including moving bins out for collection.

• Maintain general cleanliness and tidiness of exterior areas.

• Remove debris, litter, leaves, and other visible clutter.

• Keep entryways, walkways, patios, driveways, and outdoor common areas presentable.

• Perform light organization and general property cleanup as needed.

• General Property Care

• Conduct basic visual inspections of property exteriors.

• Identify and report visible maintenance issues, damage, or items requiring additional attention.

• Ensure outdoor areas are orderly and presentable.

• Identify opportunities for preventative cleanup or general upkeep.

• Periodic Cleaning & Projects

• Assist with occasional power washing of patios, walkways, driveways, and other exterior surfaces.

• Coordinate periodic window cleaning.

• Support seasonal property cleanup and organization.

• Complete other light property care projects as requested.

• Communication & Reporting

• Provide photo documentation of completed visits when appropriate.

• Communicate property concerns or maintenance needs to the Pacaso team.

• Maintain a consistent weekly service schedule.

• Notify the appropriate team members of any urgent property concerns.

Qualifications

• Previous experience in property maintenance, groundskeeping, porter services, landscaping, or general property care preferred.

• Reliable transportation and ability to travel between multiple Park City properties.

• Ability to work independently and manage a recurring service schedule.

• Strong attention to detail and pride in maintaining high-quality residential properties.

• Comfortable with basic tools and outdoor cleaning equipment.

• Ability to perform physical tasks, including lifting trash bins, carrying supplies, and general outdoor cleanup.

• Professional, responsive, and dependable.

Compensation & Engagement

• $30 per hour.

• Independent contractor engagement, subject to applicable worker-classification requirements.

• Flexible scheduling with recurring weekly service expectations.

• Hours will vary based on property needs and the scope of work.

• Specialty services or larger projects may be coordinated and approved separately.

What Success Looks Like

• All properties receive consistent weekly attention.

• Trash and recycling are managed reliably.

• Exterior and/or indoor spaces remain clean, organized, and presentable.

• Property issues are identified and communicated proactively.

• Pacaso’s Park City homes maintain a consistently high standard of care and presentation.

Why You'll Love Working Here

We invest in our Crew the way we invest in our homes — thoughtfully, generously, and with care.

• Competitive base salary and meaningful equity — every Crew member shares in what we're building

• Discretionary time off — take the rest you need, when you need it

• Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family

• Sponsored memberships to One Medical, Peloton, and WellHub for whole-person, modern healthcare

• 401(k) to help you build long-term security

• Paid parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers

• Home office stipend and a monthly internet and cell phone reimbursement to set you up for great remote work

• Quarterly team gatherings and ongoing learning and development investment

Our Commitment

Pacaso is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ability, and background — including veterans and individuals with disabilities. We believe a Crew as diverse as the owners we serve makes Pacaso stronger, and we're committed to building a workplace where every voice belongs.

• Customize messaging to clearly articulate Jama Connect’s value based on each prospect’s business needs, priorities, and buying context.

• Gather and analyze market intelligence to identify prospect trends, emerging needs, and opportunities for targeted outreach.

• Participate in regular planning, strategy, and training meetings with the industry team to align priorities and strengthen sales execution.

• Model effective sales practices, maintain accurate opportunity records, and support consistent pipeline hygiene.

• Demonstrated expertise assessing complex enterprise challenges and translating them into clear, actionable solutions supported by Jama Software and related services.

• Proven success partnering with internal teams to strengthen territory strategy and advance opportunities.

• Track record of resilience and persistence in overcoming obstacles and delivering positive outcomes.

• Strong capability to manage time and territory effectively to drive business results.

• 5+ years of proven enterprise sales experience.

• Experience selling across multiple organizational levels, including C-suite or executive sponsors, and across functions such as product, marketing, and IT.

• Knowledge of Systems Engineering and Application Lifecycle Management markets.

• Track record of achieving quotas and goals.

• Proven track record of developing mentors or champions within customer accounts.

Nice to Have:

• Experience with Systems Engineering, ALM, PLM, or RM.

• Experience in one or more of the following verticals: Aerospace and Defense, Medical Device and Life Sciences, Automotive and Semiconductor, Industrial Consumer Electronics, or SoftTech.

• Virtual first and culturally diverse work environment spanning 8 countries.

• Ambitious and fun work with a chance to define distinct, company-shaping tangible contributions.

• Comprehensive and affordable medical, dental and vision plans with pre-tax savings accounts and a generous 401(k) employer match.
