jobs.title: Senior Manager of FP&A
jobs.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Manager of FP&A at Fluidstack, you will be a cornerstone of our Finance leadership team, owning the financial planning, analysis, and decision-support infrastructure that powers one of the fastest-moving companies in AI. You will lead the full FP&A function — from annual planning and budgeting to long-range financial modeling, scenario analysis, and board-level reporting — all while building processes from the ground up. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves with urgency, and understands that great FP&A is as much about influencing decisions as it is about accuracy.



You will partner deeply with Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Finance to translate business strategy into financial clarity, and you will be instrumental in preparing Fluidstack for the next phase of its growth.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own Fluidstack’s annual operating plan, quarterly forecasting cycles, and long-range financial model across all business units and geographies.

 - Build and lead a world-class FP&A team, establishing the infrastructure, cadence, and culture of financial rigor the business needs to scale.

 - Partner with executive leadership team to develop and pressure-test strategic financial scenarios, capital allocation decisions, and growth investments.

 - Drive board and investor reporting — translating complex operational data into clear, compelling financial narratives.

 - Embed FP&A as a true business partner across Engineering, Operations, Sales, and Finance — owning the P&L bridge and variance analysis end-to-end.

 - Lead IPO readiness efforts from an FP&A perspective, including development of public-company-grade financial reporting processes and controls.

 - Own the build-out of FP&A systems and tooling, including integration with ERP platforms (NetSuite) and data infrastructure.

 - Develop KPI frameworks and financial performance dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into business health.




BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years of progressive FP&A experience, including prior experience in a senior leadership role.

 - Proven track record building and leading FP&A functions at high-growth technology, infrastructure, or pre-IPO companies.

 - Deep expertise in financial modeling, budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning in complex, multi-entity environments.

 - Experience partnering directly with C-suite and board-level stakeholders on financial strategy and reporting.

 - Strong command of ERP systems; NetSuite proficiency required.

 - Demonstrated ability to hire, develop, and lead high-performing finance teams.

 - Exceptional communication skills — you can distill complex financial data into clear insights for both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; CPA or CFA preferred.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience at a data center, infrastructure, AI/ML, or capital-intensive technology company.

 - Prior exposure to IPO readiness, S-1 preparation, or public company financial reporting standards.

 - Familiarity with multi-currency and multi-jurisdictional financial environments.

 - Experience implementing or scaling FP&A tooling and systems in partnership with engineering or data teams.

 - Big 4 or investment banking background as a complement to industry experience.




SALARY & BENEFITS

 - Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

 - Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance.

 - Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.



Total compensation may also include equity in the form of restricted stock units.

jobs.title: Associate Scientist, Protein Sciences
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.description:
Septerna is a biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, CA on a mission to develop life-changing medicines for patients with the vision to become the industry-leading G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-focused drug discovery company. The company’s Native Complex Platform™ recapitulates GPCRs with their native structure, function, and dynamics outside of the cellular context. This approach enables novel access to modern structural and screening technologies used in industrial-scale drug discovery for the entire class of GPCRs. Septerna has an emerging pipeline of GPCR-targeted small molecule programs, many in the Endocrinology space, with potential for growth to target many GPCRs that have been undruggable and unexploited to date.

We are excited to expand our multidisciplinary team of individuals focused on creating revolutionary medicines to address the unmet needs of patients. At Septerna we strive to embrace diversity of thought, expertise, and background through collaboration. To join our ambitious team, be prepared to bring your real self to work every day; grow and learn from a talented team of drug hunters, scientists, and business professionals; and contribute your passion, creativity, and energy to accomplish our mission. We share a fearless pursuit of ground-breaking innovations and cultivate an environment where our employees succeed by learning from each other and working as a team.

We are committed to the development of meaningful therapeutics for patients with indications of high unmet need. This is a tremendous opportunity to work with talented individuals on the frontlines of therapeutic discovery and development. You will directly help move therapies through preclinical research, positioning them for success in the clinic. The successful candidate will add their passion, unique talents, and expertise to a dynamic team motivated to discover new disease-modifying therapeutics for patients in a fast-paced environment.

For more information see: www.septerna.com.

About The Role

We are seeking passionate and creative individuals who want to contribute to Septerna’s mission to utilize innovative drug discovery technologies for GPCR targets. The ideal candidate will have experience in eukaryotic cell culture of suspension-based cell lines including HEK293, including cell line maintenance, transfection, and protein expression.

The chosen candidate will be working in a collaborative team contributing to improvements in protein expression and purification to support production and characterization of proteins for use in structural biology, biophysics, and small molecule drug discovery.  This position offers the unique opportunity to join an innovative well-funded biotechnology company and to contribute to its long-term success.

The position is based in South San Franscisco, CA.  Title and compensation commensurate with experience.

Responsibilities

• Perform as a hands-on cell culturist to help fully enable Septerna’s Native Complex™

• Carry out continuous cell line maintenance primarily on Expi293 suspension cell lines, but also of insect cell lines when required.

• Perform transient transfections, stable pool selection, and cell line cryopreservation of Expi293 cell lines.

• Carry out small- and large-scale cell culture for production of recombinant proteins

• Assist when needed with protein purification and protein-related assay technologies including ELISAs, SDS-PAGE, and DSF.

• Work collaboratively with Discovery Biology teams in ensuring proper prioritization and timelines of cell culture requests.

• Laboratory notebooking, data analysis and documentation.

Qualifications

• BS/MS with a minimum of 4+ years of hands-on relevant experience in a biotechnology or pharmaceutical setting.

• 1+ years demonstrated expertise in high-quality mammalian cell culture of suspension cell lines including HEK293, preferably using the Expi293 system.

• Experience in transient transfection, cell line maintenance, cell counting, stable pool selection, and cell cryopreservation.

• Prior experience with ELISA assays and basic protein techniques (SDS-PAGE, Nanodrop, DSF) is desirable.

• Ability to organize multiple projects to ensure delivery of reagents with appropriate prioritization and timelines

• Demonstrated experience working collaboratively in a team-oriented environment

• Clear and effective verbal and written communication skills

The anticipated salary range for candidates who will work in South San Francisco, CA is $100,000 - $110,000. Individual pay may vary based on additional factors, including, and without limitation, job-related skills, experience, work location and relevant education or training. Septerna's compensation package also includes benefits, stock options, and annual target bonus for full-time positions.

Note to Employment Agencies: Please do not forward any agency resumes. The company will not be responsible for any fees related to resumes that are unsolicited.  We are an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability status.  Septerna participates in the E-Verify program.  California Consumer Privacy Act Privacy Notice For Job Applicants.  If you are a California resident, click here for our CCPA Notice.

They will work independently and collaboratively in an inter-disciplinary setting to design and execute experiments in preclinical models to understand in vivo pharmacology, establish PK/PD relationships, and inform the efficacy of Septerna’s therapeutic candidates.  They will help generate and analyze functional in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo data to determine the therapeutic mechanism of action, and rank candidates for preclinical development.  They may also engage in biomarker discovery efforts by utilizing a variety of in vitro, in vivo and ex vivo models to enable and inform effective therapeutic development.  This role is expected to be primarily in the lab with some desk work.

• Be a member of multiple project teams and present results in lab, team and department meetings

• Perform in literature searches, read and interpret papers to help design and trouble-shoot in vivo and in vitro experiments

• Follow all company policies/practices, and maintain accurate records and notebooks

• Demonstrated ability to be hands on and work directly with rodent models (mice and rats), including multiple routes of administration (e.g. oral, subcutaneous, intraperitoneal, intravenous, intramuscular) and sample collection (e.g. submandibular bleed, tail vein bleed, cardiac puncture, etc).

• Experience working with other scientists to analyze, interpret, and present data

• Ability to collaborate in writing protocols and trouble-shooting biological experiments

• Detail-oriented and organized, with strong interpersonal skills for clear and effective communication – ability to proactively engage and collaboration with colleagues

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Why work at Higgsfield AI? 

Higgsfield AI is the fastest-scaling generative AI company in history, hitting $1B in annual revenue run rate, 30M+ users worldwide, 6M+ generations per day, and powering 390 of Fortune 500 brands.

We're building at the absolute frontier of AI-powered video creation and next-generation creative tools. Joining Higgsfield means becoming part of a high-impact team shaping the future of AI-native experiences, at a company that isn't just moving fast, but rewriting what fast looks like.

About the role: 

We're looking for a Data Engineer, B2B & GTM to build and scale the data infrastructure powering Higgsfield's enterprise business and go-to-market operations.

This role will own the development of reliable data pipelines, integrations, and data models that connect our product usage, customer, sales, and revenue data. You'll work closely with Sales, Revenue Operations, Finance, and Product to establish a trusted foundation for reporting, forecasting, customer intelligence, and strategic decision-making.

This is a hands-on engineering role with significant ownership and the opportunity to build scalable data systems in a rapidly growing B2B business.

What you'll do:

 - Design, develop, and maintain scalable data pipelines integrating CRM, billing, product analytics, and other business-critical systems.

 - Connect product usage, account activity, sales pipeline, contracts, and revenue data to create a consistent view of B2B customers.

 - Build reliable, well-documented data models supporting pipeline analytics, revenue reporting, customer segmentation, retention, and expansion.

 - Partner with Sales, RevOps, and Finance to support forecasting, territory planning, account prioritization, sales performance, and revenue attribution.

 - Establish visibility into how enterprise customers adopt and use Higgsfield's products, enabling insights into conversion, engagement, and expansion opportunities.

 - Implement automated validation, monitoring, documentation, and governance to ensure data accuracy and consistency across systems.

 - Identify opportunities to improve pipeline performance, automation, and infrastructure as the business grows.

Requirements:

 - 6-8+ years of experience in Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or a closely related technical role.

 - Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, with experience building production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines.

 - Experience working with modern data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift.

 - Hands-on experience with data transformation and orchestration tools such as dbt, Airflow, Dagster, or similar technologies.

 - Experience integrating data from business systems such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, or other CRM and billing platforms.

 - Strong understanding of data modeling, data architecture, and data quality best practices.

 - Familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics, including ARR, pipeline, conversion, retention, churn, and expansion.

 - Ability to translate ambiguous business requirements into scalable technical solutions.

 - Strong communication skills and experience partnering directly with nontechnical stakeholders.
   

Compensation & Benefits

 - We offer a competitive and thoughtfully structured compensation package designed to align with impact, experience, and long-term growth.

 - Base Salary: The anticipated salary range for this role is $200,000 - $260,000, depending on experience, skills, scope, and location.

 - Bonus: This role is Bonus eligible and may participate in the Company's discretionary annual bonus program.

 - Equity: In addition to cash compensation, employees are eligible to participate in the company’s stock option program and share in Higgsfield’s long-term growth.

 - Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees professionally and personally, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a competitive 401(k) retirement plan with company matching, and additional benefits and perks.

 - The opportunity to work on ambitious AI products alongside a highly experienced, fast-moving, and international team.

 - Significant ownership, direct impact, and opportunities for professional growth as the company scales.

This is a hybrid role based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Team members are expected to work from our San Francisco office three full days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely and are expected to be available during agreed working hours and to maintain sufficient overlap with the relevant team’s time zone. We value in-person collaboration, active communication, responsiveness, and close partnership across teams.

Higgsfield AI is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Senior Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

This Design Engineer role involves bridging design and production, creating and optimizing innovative product designs for manufacturability, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and ensuring compliance with internal and industry standards.

This role works in collaboration with other integrated project team (IPT) members to produce, review and mature high quality technical documentation, including CAD models, drawings, PMI’s, DFMEA’s, bills of material, and engineering specifications.

The role’s expertise in CAD, GD&T, and PLM systems ensures that engineering design intent is implemented in a manner that is accurate, functional, and manufacturable, meeting customer expectations and Divergent’s standards for quality and consistency.

The Role

• Challenge existing design requirements and define new design standards for product functions and features, based on regulations, DFM/DFAM, and product attributes.

• Act as SME for PLM, GD&T, CAD-design best practices and lesson learned.

• Ensure all designs meet required engineering, manufacturability, and industry standards, addressing issues during the release phase.

• Accountable and responsible for protecting the quality of the final engineering products (released designs, CAD, Drawings, & PMI), ensuring the production team receives data that meets quality and usability standards.

• Check technical documentation (incl. drawings, PMI, BOM’s, DFMEA, specs, etc.) before being released into PLM, enforcing compliance to internal SOP and guidelines.

• Analyze drawings, models, and documentation for GD&T accuracy, completeness, manufacturability, assemble-ability and inspectability.

• Support active programs by creating and managing design engineering data, as requested by the IPT.

• Manage ongoing production NCR’s and dispositions, collaborating with ME’s and RE’s.

• Support the implementation of ECR/ECO’s for production parts, as required or needed.

• Work cross-functionally to implement cost reduction, methods and product improvements, and support prototype and production build activities.

• Identify opportunities for standardization, automation, and process improvement in GD&T and PMI practices.

• Support the training of new personnel for the area of competence.

• Maintain and organize design documentation and reference material, ensuring all revisions and updates are properly documented, stored, and disseminated to the broader team.

Basic Qualifications

• Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.

• BS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.

• Aerospace or automotive design background.

• 2+ years of CAD experience creating detailed models.

• 2+ years of PLM/PDM experience.

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing and assembly methods, GD&T, and tolerance/stack-up analysis.

• Experience with PMI, DFMEA, control plans, PPAP and APQP.

• Experience with ASME Y14.100, Y14.5, Y14.41.

• Self-motivated with strong multi-tasking, organizational, communication and documentation skills.

• Ability to work well in an integrated team including daily interactions with technicians, engineers, and managers.

• Attention to detail and record keeping.

Preferred Qualifications

• MS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.

• 2+ years of Siemens NX experience.

• 2+ years of Teamcenter experience.

• Experience interfacing with engineering, manufacturing and quality teams to understand system designs and the associated constraints.

• Experience in CMM programming in a CNC machine shop (Mills, Lathes & EDM).

• Experience with fast iteration prototyping programs.

• Demonstrated development and configuration management experience on technically complex hardware products.

• Expertise in design for manufacturability and design for assembly including experience taking products from prototype design to production.

• Solid understanding of common manufacturing materials and processes, including mills, lathes, welding, sheet-metal bending, lifting/rigging, assembly, inspection, etc. Additive manufacturing is a plus.

• Working knowledge of all chassis systems and vehicle dynamics fundamentals.

• Proficiency in Atlassian tools (Confluence, JIRA).

Work Environment

• Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboards.

Compensation

At Divergent, our pay range is based on the level of the job. For this role, we will consider candidates at levels E03 - E05 as evaluated through our interview process.

• E03 / Engineer I: $105,980 - $145,730

• E04 / Engineer II: $122,430 - $168,340

• E05 / Senior Engineer: $141,380 - $194,390

Pay Range

$105,980—$194,390 USD

What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees:

• Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

• Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

• Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

• Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.

• Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.

Equal Employment Opportunity
Divergent is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected characteristic. Divergent provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Product Infrastructure
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.



Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.



ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.



We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.




ABOUT THE TEAM

You’ll join the core Platform & Infrastructure product org. This team builds the foundational systems and services that serve as the backbone for features across our entire product suite.

While many infrastructure teams operate behind the scenes, ours sits at an intersection. We build systems that internal vertical teams depend on, and we also deliver features that directly touch end users (e.g. platforms, self-service tools, dashboards). Because of that, you’ll balance deep technical rigor with customer empathy.

We operate in a high-growth, high-authenticity engineering culture. You’ll partner with senior engineers, architects, and cross-functional leads, and have high visibility across the org.




RESPONSIBILITIES

As a Senior Product Manager, Infrastructure & Platform, you will:

 - Define and own the roadmap for one or more core infrastructure domains (such as notification platform, documents platform, user management, etc.)

 - Deeply engage with internal stakeholders (engineering leads, vertical PMs, operations) and our customers to drive discovery and specification

 - Drive initiatives end-to-end: from ideation, discovery, scoping, to launch, adoption, and iteration

 - Work directly with customers/stakeholders (sometimes on-site at their operations) so that your deliverables are finely tuned to their unique and complex processes

 - Ensure infrastructure is resilient, scalable, observable, and secure — balancing performance, reliability, and long-term extensibility

 - Lead discovery for complex customer processes: conduct customer interviews and complete process mapping across multiple customers of varying profiles

 - Deep ability to map processes and systems even in high ambiguity — e.g. you can take a domain with many moving pieces and build a reliable abstraction

 - Write clear, structured product specs, user stories that are easy to understand, even for someone without any domain knowledge

 - Partner closely with engineering leadership and architects to make tradeoffs on design, performance, scale, and technical debt

 - Evangelize infrastructure best practices across the organization and influence roadmap tradeoffs




IDEAL BACKGROUND

 - 5+ years of product management (or equivalent) experience, ideally with exposure to b2b saas products, product infrastructure, and platforms

 - Strong technical fluency: experience working with engineers around systems, APIs, data models, etc. 

 - Excellent customer discovery skills: comfortable conducting interviews, writing journey maps, and synthesizing qualitative + quantitative inputs

 - Track record of shipping infrastructure or platform features that were adopted broadly or had measurable impact

 - Highly structured thinker, able to write and communicate complex concepts simply

 - Comfortable operating with high autonomy, ambiguity, and responsibility

 - Strong collaboration skills: able to manage stakeholders, drive alignment, and hold cross-team accountability

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, or a closely related field




WHY JOIN VALON?

 - Transform a $13 trillion industry by building the operating system for mortgage servicing, replacing 40-year-old legacy systems with modern, AI-powered infrastructure

 - Join at a pivotal moment: We're rapidly scaling, with contracts signed or in negotiation representing nearly 30% of the entire mortgage servicing market

 - Work on complex, high-impact problems with massive scale, our platform will power servicing operations for millions of homeowners across the country

 - Product and Engineering-led culture with exceptional talent density, work alongside world-class engineers and product leaders who value velocity, clarity, and deep technical excellence

 - Real product ownership with enterprise impact: your decisions will directly influence how major financial institutions operate and serve their customers

 - Unique market position: We're winning against entrenched incumbents by delivering 75%+ cost reduction and a modern software experience that were previously not possible




BENEFITS

 - Compensation: competitive salary with a meaningful stake in the company via equity, and 401(k) plan. The base salary range reflects multiple levels. We assess level based on a combination of experience and interview performance.

 - Health & well-being: we’ll invest in your physical and mental well-being with comprehensive medical, dental, & vision benefits.

 - Free Food: daily lunch, and dinner provided through Forkable for in-office team members.

 - Commuter benefits: pre-tax deductions for public transit, rideshares, and parking to simplify your daily commute.

 - Grow together: company wide orientation for you to successfully onboard and other learning & development opportunities including regular review cycles that feature 360-degree feedback.

 - Play together: quarterly budgets for team and company outings. Use it for team swag, cooking classes, or team dinners.

 - Generous time off: flexible paid time off with no annual limit, sick days, and 11 company holidays.

 - Baby bonding time: 12 weeks of fully paid leave for both birthing and non-birthing parents, so you can spend uninterrupted time welcoming and caring for your newest family member.



Throughout the interview process, please remember that emails will only be from valon.com http://valon.com email addresses. We will never ask for any personally identifiable information during the interview process itself. Please reach out to talent@valon.com if you have any requests to verify the authenticity of an outreach.



Valon is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Valon makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs at the time.

jobs.title: Director of Materials Management
jobs.description:
Who we are

Neros is a defense technology company rebuilding America’s drone industrial base. We design and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are tested in combat, iterated at startup speed, and built at massive scale. Our team culture is fast, hands-on, and obsessed with closing the gap between design and deployment.

As drones transform the character of warfare, Neros is delivering the systems the West needs to compete on the modern battlefield and deter the adversaries of democracy. We’re hiring engineers, operators, and builders who want to move fast, take on extreme ownership, and get capability into the hands of warfighters in months, not years.

What you will be doing

As Director of Materials Management, you will own all material flow at Neros: inventory and warehousing, shipping and receiving, kitting and line-side replenishment, fulfillment, and logistics. Your team is responsible for every part from the receiving dock to the production line and every finished drone from pack-out to delivery, with inventory accuracy and material availability as the core mandates. This is both an operations leadership and an engineering role: you will design and continuously redesign warehouse layouts, material flow systems, and packaging standards as production rate scales, build and lead a multi-shift team that will grow to include industrial and packaging engineers, and plan the capital investments and execute projects required to support production of over 1M drones per year in our 250k sqft Torrance factory.

Responsibilities

• Own all inventory, material handling, and warehouse operations: process, systems, and execution

• Ensure everything gets shipped on-time every time, including total ownership of the fulfillment and shipping functions for both standard product and one-off shipments (including hazmat)

• Maintain high inventory accuracy through process control and routine cycle counting, meeting internal and external audit requirements

• Define packaging, kitting, internal transport, and line-side presentation standards at the part-number level in partnership with production and supply chain

• Design warehouse layouts, storage systems, and material flow for each rate increase; plan and execute capital investments in racking, material handling equipment, and automation

• Use simulation and data analysis to continuously improve the floorplan, processes, tooling, and training and increase overall efficiency per employee

• Hire, develop, and lead a multi-level, multi-shift organization of hourly and salaried team members, with a safety-first floor culture

• Partner with supply chain and business systems teams to develop tools and systems to visualize and execute work reliably, and enable processes such as FIFO, Kanban, clear-to-build, fulfillment, and more

You should have the following

• 8+ years in materials management, warehouse, or distribution operations inside a manufacturing plant, including 3+ years managing teams

• Owned inventory accuracy for an operation with 1,000+ active part numbers

• Transaction-level fluency in an ERP/WMS system — min/max settings, backflush, cycle count variance, and location management

Nice to have

jobs.title: Cloud Systems Administrator
jobs.description:
Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

The Systems Administrator owns the day-to-day administration of our SaaS and cloud vendor stack, with security and logging as the first priority. You will manage user access across every platform we use, keep audit logging and security controls configured and reviewed, write scripts to automate repetitive admin work, and act as a first responder on security incidents. You will also provide hands-on IT support to employees. This is a generalist role for someone who likes owning systems end to end: you are the person who knows how each vendor is set up, who has access to what, and where the logs live.

What you'll do:

Vendor and SaaS administration (security and logging first)

• Serve as the primary administrator for our SaaS and cloud platforms: tenant settings, SSO/SAML and SCIM integration, MFA enforcement, API keys, roles and permissions.

• Configure and maintain audit logging on every platform that supports it; centralize logs where possible and make sure retention meets our compliance needs.

• Run periodic access reviews, remove stale accounts and over-privileged roles, and keep an accurate inventory of who has admin rights where.

• Own the security posture of each vendor: review security settings on new tools before rollout, track vendor security notices, and evaluate new vendor requests for risk.

User lifecycle and identity

• Onboard and offboard employees and contractors across all systems the same day, driven from Rippling and Google Workspace, our identity sources of truth.

• Manage groups, roles and licenses; keep license counts right-sized and flag waste.

• Maintain device enrollment, MDM policies and endpoint security for company laptops.

Scripting and automation

• Write and maintain scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and use vendor APIs to automate provisioning, access reviews, log collection and reporting.

• Build lightweight integrations between systems (for example, HRIS to identity provider to SaaS) so manual admin work shrinks over time.

Security incident response

• Act as a first responder on security alerts: triage, contain (disable accounts, revoke tokens, isolate devices), gather evidence from logs, and escalate.

• Participate in post-incident reviews and implement the fixes that come out of them.

• Help maintain and test our incident response and business continuity runbooks.

IT support

• Provide tier 1–2 support to employees: hardware, accounts, access, video conferencing, printers and office network.

• Procure, image and manage laptops and peripherals; keep an asset inventory current.

• Write and keep up internal how-to documentation so common requests become self-service.

Platforms you will administer

These are our largest software and cloud vendors by spend over the last 12 months. Deep experience with the first group is expected; the rest you will pick up on the job.

Area

Platforms

Cloud infrastructure

Amazon Web Services (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub)

Identity, HR and devices

Rippling (HRIS, SSO, device management) and Google Workspace, used together as our identity source of truth

Productivity and email

Google Workspace (admin console, Vault, security center)

Customer support and CRM

Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom

Communications

Zoom, Aircall, Twilio

Data and engineering

Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, Sentry, Linear, Postman, Stytch

AI platforms

Anthropic, OpenAI (API key and usage management)

Collaboration and design

Notion, Lucid, Figma, Adobe, Scribe

Security tools

NordVPN Teams, Virtru (email encryption)

Healthcare operations

Waystar, AdvancedMD

Marketing and recruiting

Braze, ActiveCampaign, Greenhouse, LinkedIn

About you:

• 3+ years administering SaaS and cloud platforms in a company of 50–500 people, including Google Workspace and an identity/HR platform like Rippling or Okta, and ideally AWS.

• Hands-on experience configuring SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA policies and role-based access.

• Working knowledge of audit logging and log review: you know what a CloudTrail event, a Workspace audit log or a Zendesk audit entry looks like and what to do with it.

• Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell or Bash, and comfort calling REST APIs.

• Experience responding to security incidents (phishing, compromised accounts, lost devices) and documenting what happened.

• Strong IT support instincts: you communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues and close tickets fast.

• Familiarity with HIPAA or a comparable compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and what it means for access control and logging.

Nice to have:

• AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, Security Specialty, or Google Workspace Administrator certification.

• Experience with a SIEM or log aggregation tool (Datadog, Splunk, Google SecOps, or similar) and writing detection rules.

• MDM experience (Rippling, Jamf, Kandji, Intune) and macOS/Windows endpoint hardening.

• Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for managing AWS and SaaS configuration.

• Prior work in a healthcare or other regulated company.

• Experience administering API usage and keys for AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI) and setting spend and access controls.

jobs.title: Senior Growth / Demand Generation Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

We're living through a fundamental shift in how people discover, evaluate, and purchase products. The next generation doesn't respond to traditional marketing -- they build relationships with brands through authentic social interactions, seek recommendations from communities they trust, and expect personalized experiences that feel human, not corporate.

At Nectar, we're building the AI-native social operating system that enables this new era of commerce. We believe every social interaction should deepen the relationship between brands and their communities while creating genuine value for both sides.

Founded by ex-Meta product and engineering leaders, we've raised over $30M in total capital from investors including GV and True Ventures. We work with brands like Oura Health, Caraway, e.l.f. Cosmetics, Kosas, OLIPOP, and many more. We're building the future of social commerce -- where community, conversation, and commerce converge.


THE ROLE

We're looking for a bold, creative Senior Growth / Demand Generation Manager to build and scale the pipeline engine behind Nectar's growth. Reporting to VP, GTM, you'll own our acquisition strategy end-to-end, from paid and organic channels to the creative ideas that make people stop scrolling, and turn our marketing spend into measurable pipeline and revenue.

Our buyers are community managers, social media managers, and CMOs at consumer brands. They live on social, can spot generic B2B marketing instantly, and trust their peers more than any ad. Winning them takes creativity as much as rigor: showing up where they already spend their time, in a voice they recognize, with campaigns worth sharing. This is a senior, high-impact role where you'll define how Nectar reaches that audience and build the demand generation function as we scale.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own Nectar's demand generation strategy and influence sales pipeline, from channel mix and budget allocation to forecasting and reporting to leadership

 - Lead paid search, social, and sponsorships and reach our champions and buyers where they already are: LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, industry communities, newsletters, podcasts, creator partnerships, and more

 - Partner with Creative to concept and launch social-first campaigns that feel native to the platforms our buyers use every day and stand out from typical B2B marketing

 - Discover, test, and scale new acquisition channels, and kill the ones that don't perform

 - Design nurture programs for new prospects and cross-sell audiences within our existing customer base

 - Analyze program performance and turn the data into recommendations that improve conversion across ads, landing pages, and the full funnel

 - Stand up an account based marketing strategy alongside sales to deliver meaningful engagement across key accounts

 - Work with revenue operations to optimize our marketing tech stack, attribution, and campaign ROI reporting
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4-7 years of growth or demand generation experience in B2B SaaS and/or AI-native companies, including ownership of a meaningful pipeline target and budget

 - A portfolio of creative, unconventional campaigns that drove measurable pipeline, not just impressions

 - Deep fluency in social platforms and the culture around them: you know how social and community teams think and what earns their attention, or can demonstrate an ability to ramp on this ICP quickly

 - Hands-on experience with AI-native tools like Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, or other LLM-powered workflows

 - Track record launching and scaling paid campaigns across LinkedIn, Google, Meta, YouTube, TikTok, and X

 - Proficiency with marketing automation, email, A/B testing, and personalization tools, plus Salesforce, Google Analytics, and more

 - Experience building a function at an early-stage company, with the judgment to operate independently and drive complex cross-functional projects to completion

 - Comfort operating in ambiguous environments in a fast-moving startup
   
   


BONUS POINTS

 - Experience in martech, social media platforms, or commerce-related software

 - Experience marketing to consumer brands or DTC marketing, social, and community teams

 - Experience running account-based marketing programs for enterprise and mid-market buyers

 - Experience working at a company through a Series A or Series B growth phase
   
   


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation and early equity

 - Health, vision, and dental benefits + 401(k) match

 - ClassPass membership for fitness and wellness classes

 - $50/month mobile stipend for all employees, and $50/month internet stipend for remote employees

For our Palo Alto Office:

 - Hybrid schedule: 4 days in office, plus 3 remote flex days per quarter (after your first 3 months)

 - Free lunch in the office

 - $1,000/month housing stipend for living near the office

 - Fully paid for commuter benefits (train stipend or Palo Alto parking reimbursement)

jobs.title: EH&S Lead
jobs.description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

• Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets, accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.

• Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs.

About you

• You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.

• You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.

• You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.

• You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

• Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.

• Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.

• Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.

• Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.

• Define Arc’s approach to EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.

• Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.

• Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.

• Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.

• Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.

• Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.

• Develop and manage EH&S management systems covering chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permitting compliance, and incident investigations.

• Oversee regulated medical and hazardous waste programs, including vendor contracting.

• Act as primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies and government authorities.

• Own procurement and maintenance of safety equipment and supply inventory, ensuring onsite personnel are adequately protected from workplace hazards.

• Respond to emergency situations involving hazardous materials.

• Develop, own and maintain Arc’s EH&S wiki.

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in industrial hygiene, biology, chemistry, environmental science, occupational safety and health, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Master’s degree preferred.

• 8+ years of laboratory experience, including 5 years in EH&S, with a minimum of 2 years leading and developing EH&S programs.

• Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a track record of managing multiple projects accurately and on time.

• Working knowledge of the scientific and technical aspects of applicable regulations — including Cal/OSHA, CalEPA, the Medical Waste Management Act, EPA, DEA, OSHA, NRC, and NFPA — and how they bear on laboratory operations.

• Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize resources, influence group behavior, and build consensus around safety practice.

• Able to work independently and as part of a dynamic team, with a positive attitude, a strong sense of urgency, and a bias toward action.

• Interest in learning new techniques, keeping accurate records, and working within established policies.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Animal Research Occupational Health and Safety programs.

• Experience supporting laboratory animal research involving biohazardous or hazardous materials.

• Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) certification.

The base salary range for this position is $127,000 to $157,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

jobs.title: Staff Nuclear Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Staff Nuclear Engineer to provide technical expertise across the nuclear design and analysis of Kaleidos. You will work across core physics, neutron and radiation transport, shielding, activation and dose, thermal-hydraulics, safety analysis, instrumentation and controls, reactor operations, and regulatory evaluations to solve multidisciplinary reactor design challenges.

This role combines deep hands-on analysis with technical ownership across major nuclear engineering workstreams. You will lead complex projects from requirements definition and early design trades through model development, analysis, verification and validation, testing, and regulatory documentation. You will help establish analytical methods and technical standards, mentor engineers, and serve as a key technical interface between nuclear analysis and the broader reactor engineering organization.

The ideal candidate brings deep technical judgment, strong engineering fundamentals, and the ability to translate complex nuclear analysis into practical reactor design decisions. You should be comfortable operating with significant technical autonomy, working across disciplines, and driving difficult engineering problems through closure.

Responsibilities & Duties

 - Provide technical leadership across reactor physics, core performance, shielding, dose and activation, thermal-hydraulics, safety analysis, I&C, and reactor operations.

 - Own complex nuclear engineering projects from requirements capture and design iteration through model development, analysis, technical review, and final documentation.

 - Perform and guide analyses of criticality, reactivity control, shutdown margin, power distribution, depletion, temperature feedback, radiation transport, dose, activation, and shielding performance.

 - Develop, review, and improve high-fidelity neutron and radiation transport models used to support reactor design, safety, testing, and regulatory evaluations.

 - Translate analytical results into actionable requirements and design decisions affecting the core, shielding, control systems, instrumentation, fluid systems, structures, and surrounding hardware.

 - Lead multidisciplinary technical trades and evaluate the interaction between nuclear performance, thermal behavior, mechanical design, controls, operations, manufacturability, and safety.

 - Establish and improve rigorous practices for model verification and validation, peer review, configuration control, uncertainty evaluation, and technical documentation.

 - Ensure analytical assumptions, limitations, uncertainties, margins, and conclusions are clearly documented and technically defensible.

 - Develop analytical methods, workflows, and tools that improve the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of Radiant’s nuclear engineering capability.

 - Collaborate with reactor systems, thermal, mechanical, electrical, test, operations, safety, and regulatory teams to resolve multidisciplinary design challenges.

 - Work with the regulatory organization to translate applicable nuclear standards and requirements into analysis plans, design criteria, calculation packages, and verification activities.

 - Support reactor testing and startup by defining analysis needs, instrumentation requirements, acceptance criteria, and methods for comparing predicted and measured performance.

 - Provide technical mentorship and review for engineers across nuclear design and analysis activities.

 - Identify technical risks, develop practical mitigation strategies, and drive complex nuclear engineering problems through closure.

 - Communicate technical status, risks, decisions, and recommendations clearly to engineering teams and company leadership.

Required Qualifications & Skills

 - Bachelor’s degree in nuclear engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.

 - 8+ years of relevant nuclear engineering experience across reactor design, analysis, testing, licensing, safety, or operations.

 - Demonstrated experience owning complex nuclear engineering projects involving multiple technical disciplines and stakeholders.

 - Deep knowledge of neutron transport theory, Monte Carlo simulation methods, nuclear data, and statistical convergence.

 - Professional experience developing and applying MCNP, OpenMC, or comparable neutron and radiation transport models.

 - Strong understanding of reactor physics concepts, including criticality, reactivity coefficients, depletion, power distribution, shutdown margin, neutron and gamma transport, and uncertainty analysis.

 - Experience translating analytical results into reactor design decisions, technical requirements, safety conclusions, or regulatory documentation.

 - Experience developing or reviewing technically rigorous analysis methodologies, models, calculation packages, or engineering standards.

 - Familiarity with model verification and validation, configuration control, peer review, and nuclear software quality practices.

 - Demonstrated ability to operate independently on technically complex problems and drive work from definition through technical closure.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex analyses, assumptions, uncertainties, and technical conclusions to multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications & Skills

 - Master’s degree or Ph.D. in nuclear engineering or a related technical discipline.

 - Subject-matter expertise in safety analysis, shielding, radiation dose and activation, instrumentation and controls, reactor operations, thermal-hydraulics, or radioactive-material transportation.

 - Experience with high-temperature gas-cooled reactors, microreactors, advanced reactors, or first-of-a-kind nuclear systems.

 - Experience with SCALE, Serpent, Shift, Griffin, MOOSE-based applications, or similar nuclear analysis tools.

 - Proficiency with Python or another language used for simulation automation, model generation, and analysis post-processing.

 - Experience with coupled neutronics and thermal-hydraulics or other multiphysics analyses.

 - Familiarity with DOE authorization processes, NRC licensing, nuclear industry codes and standards, or regulatory safety analysis.

 - Experience supporting reactor testing, commissioning, startup, or operational readiness.

 - Experience developing analytical methods, technical standards, or nuclear engineering capabilities within a growing engineering organization.

 - Demonstrated experience mentoring engineers and providing technical review across complex engineering programs.

Additional Requirements

 - Must be mission driven and willing to support extended hours when needed.

 - Must work 100% onsite at Radiant’s El Segundo headquarters.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Corporate Paralegal to join our collaborative legal team. • Coordinate with outside counsel on various corporate, transactional, and litigation matters

What You Need:

• 6+ years of paralegal experience, including at least 2+ years supporting a publicly traded company (in-house or at a law firm)

• Exceptional attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines

At Archer we aim to attract, retain, and motivate talent that possess the skills and leadership necessary to grow our business. In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance& punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.
Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
Prepare product.
Receive and process telephone orders.
Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.
Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.
Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.
Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.
Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.
Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

jobs.title: Manager, FSQA
jobs.description:
The Manager, FSQA is responsible for leading Food Safety, Quality Assurance, Supplier Quality, and Regulatory Compliance programs to ensure the consistent delivery of safe, high-quality products across the supply chain. This role partners closely with operations, procurement, suppliers, and cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement, strengthen food safety culture, and ensure compliance with company standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

What You'll Do

• Lead and maintain Food Safety and Quality Management Systems to ensure compliance with company, customer, regulatory, and GFSI requirements.
• Oversee product quality and compliance for assigned product categories across the U.S. and Canadian supply chain, ensuring ingredients meet Domino’s standards, customer expectations, and applicable regulatory requirements.
• Own and maintain product specifications and supplier documentation for assigned categories, including product attributes, organoleptic characteristics, physical measures, analytical measures, and regulatory requirements.
• Lead product reviews and ongoing product performance evaluations, including organoleptic and analytical assessments, trend analysis, reporting, and follow-up actions with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
• Manage product quality incidents and complaint management processes for assigned categories, including intake, investigation, root cause analysis, supplier corrective actions, escalation, communication, and timely closure.
• Serve as the organization’s subject matter expert for Cheese/Dairy quality and food safety, providing technical guidance to suppliers, Procurement, R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, and FSQA teams.
• Oversee supplier quality programs, including supplier approval, risk assessments, audits, corrective actions, and performance monitoring.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives related to food safety, quality performance, sanitation, environmental monitoring, and risk reduction.
• Partners with Operations, Procurement, R&D, and Supply Chain teams to ensure product quality and food safety requirements are integrated into business processes.
• Provide technical guidance and coaching to cross-functional teams and suppliers to strengthen food safety culture, product quality, and compliance.
• Identify opportunities to leverage technology and analytics to improve the overall quality and safety of Domino’s food.

• Bachelor’s degree in food science or related field; Master’s preferred
• 7+ years of quality assurance or related experience, in food manufacturing, or research and development
• Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills across functions and all organizational levels
• Able to identify opportunities, set goals, and work independently
• Extensive knowledge of cheese/dairy products preferred.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills
• Ability to communicate with suppliers, internal leadership, and team members
• Strong statistical analysis skills
• HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) certification and strong knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices, Good Laboratory Practices, Standard Sanitation Operating Procedures, preferred
• Able to manage multiple projects and manage time effectively with minimal guidance.
• Excellent knowledge of computer skills including MS Office suite of programs
• Availability to be on call to support product incident responses outside of normal business hours including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
• Travel up to 30% of the time

Benefits:

•    Paid Holidays and Vacation

•    Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment

•    No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents

•    Childcare tuition discounts

•    No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs

•    Fertility benefits

•    Adoption assistance

•    401k matching contributions

•    15% off the purchase price of stock

•    Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

You must be 18 years of age and have a valid driver's license with a safe driving record meeting company standards as well as access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery. Operate all equipment.
Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, and walk-in cooler. Prepare product.
Receive and process telephone orders.
Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
Clean equipment and facility daily.

TRAINING
Orientation and training provided on the job.

COMMUNICATION SKILLS

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.
Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area. Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

Talking and hearing on telephone.
Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Of course, you'll need some skills- judgement, math and the ability to multi-task.

Assistant managers are responsible for everything that happens during the shift. This includes cost control, inventory control, cash control and customer relations. You set the tone and the example for the store and you have to be on your game 100% of the time!

Your job responsibilities would include (but are not limited to):
